evidence.note: TaskCreate markers structure coarse phases: explore+baseline MVP tests first, then a dedicated MVP-fix task (Call/CallIndirect/numeric/validation), then completion — a genuine MVP-vs-SIMD separation (anchor 5).

Front-loaded shared infrastructure: designed v128 lane accessors for all lane widths early and wrote simd.rs with a unary/binary dispatch so later ops are thin wrappers — an element of the top anchor.
SIMD implemented monolithically (all enum variants, all 0xFD decoding, whole op file in single passes) rather than as an ordered, dependency-respecting family sequence — falls short of anchor 8.

Family-level work (const, conversions, select, bitwise, lane, boolean) surfaced reactively as the aggregate runner flagged failing suites; spec JSON files acted as done-signals but as test-driven triage, not a pre-planned milestone list.
Done-vs-remaining tracked implicitly via repeated full-suite runs identifying suites with N failures; no explicit live milestone/todo list maintained.

reasoning: The agent clearly separated the MVP-fix phase from SIMD and used per-family spec JSON files as done-signals, satisfying anchor 5, and it also front-loaded genuine shared infrastructure (v128 lane accessors + unary/binary dispatch) which is a hallmark of the top anchor. However, the SIMD surface was implemented in one monolithic push and then debugged reactively file-by-file rather than sequenced into an explicit, dependency-respecting ordered family hierarchy, and no live milestone tracker was kept. This places it between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.
